subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a `gateway.peers` and raw `gatewayUrl` session-tool routing surface now, or wait for an approved federation/peer-identity contract before adding cross-gateway session messaging?
rationale: The requested workflow is real, but this PR changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and config/API surface in ways automation cannot safely choose for maintainers.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define peer identity, allowed URLs, token scope, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing a core implementation.

options.title: Narrow to an approved remote target
options.body: Allow only an explicitly configured and security-reviewed remote target path, removing raw model-supplied gateway URLs until a broader peer contract exists.

options.title: Pause for the federation FRD
options.body: Leave this PR unmerged while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 settles the bridge protocol and identity model.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, allowed URLs, token scope, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing a core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history trail covers the session-tool owner boundary and gateway URL/security policy this decision would change.
